requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the exact specified ed25519 public key installed for SSH access
requirements.summary: id opsadmin confirms the account exists (uid 1001) and cat authorized_keys shows the exact key 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINMKA2+oNHxgmpABaV61Sar8lVW2YxSL8Aw9d7b5yLh1 os-comparison@example.invalid' present, with correct 700/600 ownership, both before (cmd-61de3116ce6d4f2b) and after (cmd-e511e3b8a7b245a3) the restart.

requirements.requirement: SSH authentication on node1 requires a key (password authentication disabled)
requirements.summary: sshd_config shows PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no with a syntactically valid config (sshd -t) and an active sshd service (cmd-9e82db8f6d0242bb). A live local ssh attempt forcing PreferredAuthentications=password is rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)' both pre-restart (cmd-a25cfa70c6d54e4b) and post-restart (cmd-e511e3b8a7b245a3), and the opsadmin account password is locked, closing the password fallback path.

requirements.requirement: Resulting sshd configuration is valid and the service remains healthy
requirements.summary: After several iterations that produced duplicate directive lines, the executor cleaned them up (cmd-375ee14abd764ff6, cmd-752aab71e4214435) leaving a single set of directives; sshd -t passes and systemctl is-active sshd reports active both pre- and post-restart (cmd-9e82db8f6d0242bb, cmd-e511e3b8a7b245a3).

requirements.requirement: Independent restart-evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/config state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf, active sshd, and opsadmin/key state (cmd-7886f392e8864086), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. Reboot was acknowledged (cmd-d572b18bd94f492f), the node was unreachable during two timed-out polls (cmd-b3cd223a24bf418f, cmd-0390bb82a6774cc0), then reachable again (cmd-03ed833299cc4204). Post-restart boot_id fe19be03-fca5-42c7-879d-fdeaf4e609bb differs from baseline and matches the fixed after_executor snapshot; sshd is active, sshd -t passes, opsadmin account and authorized_keys persisted, and password auth is still rejected (cmd-e511e3b8a7b245a3).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — opsadmin created with the exact specified public key and SSH restricted to key-based authentication — are directly satisfied by both pre- and post-restart evidence, including a live password-auth rejection test. The independent node-restart protocol also shows a clean pre/post boot-identity transition with recovered service and data state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall but not perfect: two failed troubleshooting attempts led to transient duplicate sshd_config directives that were properly cleaned up, and one sshd_config backup file was left behind without confirmation of removal.
limitations: No independent verification that the leftover sshd_config.bak.<timestamp> file was ever removed; its presence/absence in final state is not directly evidenced.

GSSAPI-based authentication (implied by the 'gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic' methods listed in the denial message) was not explicitly checked or disabled; in practice it requires Kerberos infrastructure not present here, so it is unlikely to provide a real bypass, but this was not directly confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two early attempts failed with no state change (cmd-4f74b516b7614a9c: python3 missing, aborted after directory/key setup; cmd-cf49c43008404de3: sed edit followed by a permission-denied grep, return_code 2). These caused the executor to iterate with sed against the config, producing duplicate directive lines across several commands (cmd-a42c5a8d833948e9 shows 6 duplicated lines at lines 141-146 plus originals), which the executor then deliberately removed via cmd-375ee14abd764ff6 and cmd-752aab71e4214435, arriving at a clean single-directive config verified in cmd-9e82db8f6d0242bb. The intermediate duplication was a self-corrected side effect of troubleshooting rather than a deliberate unnecessary mutation, and left no residue in the final state. One residual artifact was not explicitly cleaned up: cmd-4f74b516b7614a9c created a timestamped backup file /etc/ssh/sshd_config.bak.<ts> before editing sshd_config; this is a bounded, low-risk, conventional safety backup, but it is not shown as removed afterward, so it is flagged as a minor leftover file rather than a security or functional issue. No other unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations are evident; the lifecycle diff shows only expected boot-id/temp-file/socket-PID changes from the reboot itself.
